title: Autoencoders
overview: An autoencoder compresses inputs into a low-dimensional code and reconstructs them. The bottleneck forces the network to learn useful structure without labels.
objectives: Build an encoder and decoder with a bottleneck
Use reconstruction loss for representation learning

method.title: Encoder and decoder
method.body: The encoder maps x to a code z; the decoder maps z back to a reconstruction x_hat.

method.title: Reconstruction loss
method.body: Training minimizes the difference between x and x_hat, such as MSE.

method.title: Bottleneck
method.body: A code smaller than the input prevents the trivial identity mapping.

method.title: Variants
method.body: Denoising autoencoders reconstruct clean inputs from corrupted ones; applications include anomaly detection.

pseudocode:
z = encoder(x)
x_hat = decoder(z)
loss = mean((x - x_hat)**2)
loss.backward(); optimizer.step()

playground.starterCode:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
Z = rng.normal(size=(200, 2))
X = Z @ rng.normal(size=(2, 6))            # 6-d data lying on a 2-d subspace
We = rng.normal(size=(6, 2)) * 0.3; Wd = rng.normal(size=(2, 6)) * 0.3
for step in range(2001):
    code = X @ We; rec = code @ Wd
    err = rec - X
    if step % 500 == 0: print(step, round(float((err ** 2).mean()), 4))
    gWd = code.T @ err * 2 / err.size
    gWe = X.T @ (err @ Wd.T) * 2 / err.size
    Wd -= 0.1 * gWd; We -= 0.1 * gWe

quiz.question: Why must the autoencoder have a bottleneck?
options: To avoid learning a trivial identity map
